title: Milano Stovetop Espresso Maker
short_description: Six-cup moka pot in cast aluminium. Gas, electric and ceramic safe.
description:
A six-cup moka pot in cast aluminium with a heat-resistant handle. Brews on gas, electric and ceramic tops; not induction unless you use a converter disc.

The gasket and filter plate are replaceable rather than glued in, so the pot outlasts its seals. Hand wash only — dishwasher detergent strips the interior patina that keeps the coffee from tasting metallic.

Ships from Ontario. Brews roughly 300 ml, which is two small cups rather than six of anything you would recognise as a mug.

title: Madrid French Press
short_description: Borosilicate carafe, 1 L, with a stainless steel filter basket.
description:
A one-litre French press with a borosilicate glass carafe and a three-part stainless filter basket. The frame is powder-coated steel and comes apart with no tools, so the whole thing can be cleaned properly rather than rinsed and hoped for.

Replacement carafes and screens are stocked separately — this is the kind of object where the glass is the part that breaks and the rest lasts a decade.

Ships from Ontario. Holds 1 L, which is four small cups of coffee at the strength most people brew.

title: Heidelberg Glass Teapot
short_description: Hand-blown borosilicate, 600 ml, with a removable glass infuser.
description:
A 600 ml teapot in hand-blown borosilicate with a glass infuser that lifts out, so leaf tea stops brewing when you decide it should rather than when the pot is empty.

Borosilicate takes direct heat, so it can go on a low gas flame or a tealight warmer without cracking. It is still glass: it will not survive being knocked off a counter.

Ships from Ontario. Each one is blown individually, so wall thickness and the exact curve of the spout vary slightly between pots.
